data.title: Losers Outnumber Gainers By Over Three Times As Selling Pressure Intensifies
data.description:
The stock market movement saw losers outnumber gainers by more than three to one on Nov 6, with 964 counters declining against just 273 advancing, as broad-based selling pressure swept across the local bourse.

At the closing bell, 404 counters were unchanged, 1,132 remained untraded and 10 were suspended, reflecting the weak market sentiment.

Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd topped the losers’ list, plunging RM2.68 to RM36.20, followed by Nestlé (M) Bhd, which shed RM1.84 to RM94.16.

Technology-related counters also faced heavy selling, with ViTrox Corporation Bhd declining 48 sen to RM10.12, while Mega Fortris Bhd tumbled 43 sen to RM1.40.

Meanwhile, Concrete Engineering Products Bhd rounded out the top five losers, falling 30 sen to RM4.40.

Despite the broader market weakness, Fraser & Neave Holdings Bhd emerged as the day’s biggest gainer, surging RM1 to RM22.22.

United Plantations Bhd followed with a 28 sen gain to RM30.38, while Carlsberg Brewery Malaysia Bhd advanced 14 sen to RM12.68.

MN Holdings Bhd and Petronas Gas Bhd also recorded gains of 12 sen each, closing at RM3.82 and RM17.42, respectively.

Total market turnover stood at 3.64 billion shares worth RM3.5 billion.

The sharp imbalance between declining and advancing stocks underscored widespread selling pressure, with selective buying in consumer, plantation and energy counters providing limited relief to the broader market.

data.title: Bursa Ends Lower As Wall Street Rout Sparks Broad Sell-Off
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia ended the week sharply lower on Nov 6, with the benchmark index shedding 19.28 points as broad-based selling gripped the market following Wall Street’s overnight rout and losses across regional bourses.

At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 19.28 points, or 1.18%, to 1,616.58 from Thursday’s close of 1,635.86, as weak global sentiment weighed on investor appetite.

The benchmark index traded between 1,610.80 and 1,620.55 throughout the session.

The broader market suffered heavier losses, with the FBM 70 plunging 333.85 points, or 1.92%, to 17,020.88, while the F4GBM declined 14.03 points, or 1.43%, to 969.95.

The FBM Emas dropped 169.37 points, or 1.40%, to 11,965.47, while the FBM Shariah lost 184.33 points, or 1.54%, to 11,822.77.

Among the most actively traded stocks, Zetrix AI Bhd topped the list, gaining half a sen to 6.5 sen on close to 247 million shares changing hand.

Inari Amertron Bhd fell 16 sen to RM2.12, while VS Industry Bhd declined 2.5 sen to 29.5 sen, reflecting continued selling pressure on technology-related counters.

Top Glove Corporation Bhd bucked the downtrend, rising two sen to 96.5 sen, while NationGate Holdings Bhd shed five sen to RM1.82.

Total market turnover stood at 3.64 billion shares worth RM3.5 billion.

The weak closing performance reflected persistent risk aversion across regional equity markets as investors reassessed exposure to technology stocks following the sharp overnight decline on Wall Street.

data.title: Nikkei Falls Below 60,000 For First Time Since May Amid AI Regulation Concerns
data.description:
Japan’s benchmark Nikkei stock index briefly plunged more than 7% on Friday, falling below the 60,000 mark for the first time since May, as concerns over tighter artificial intelligence (AI) regulations in the United States weighed on technology shares.

The sell-off followed overnight losses on Wall Street, where technology stocks tumbled amid concerns that Democratic gains in the US midterm elections could lead to tighter restrictions on data centre construction, potentially curbing investment in AI infrastructure.

At the morning close, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average had shed 3,219.29 points, or 5.27%, to 57,858.61 from Thursday’s close.

The broader Topix index also fell 213.89 points, or 5.43%, to 3,726.50.

Beyond technology shares, broader selling across the Japanese market reflected growing uncertainty over the economic and political outlook, according to analysts.

The concerns come amid heavy investment in data centres and AI infrastructure, with potential regulatory changes raising questions over the pace of future development and capital spending.

data.title: RHB Reverses Bearish Stance On Gold, Sees Moving To US$4,200
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank has reversed its bearish stance on COMEX gold futures and initiated long positions after the precious metal broke above the key US$4,100 resistance level, signalling renewed bullish momentum.

In its latest technical analysis report, RHB said gold futures extended their rally for a second consecutive session on Thursday (Nov 5), rising US$40.50 to close at US$4,113.50 per ounce.

The commodity opened at US$4,075.40 before trading between an intraday low of US$4,067 and a high of US$4,155.80.

RHB said the bullish candlestick and gold’s move above its 20-day simple moving average (SMA) indicated that the short-term trend had turned positive.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) also climbed above the 50-point threshold, reinforcing expectations of continued upward momentum.

RHB expects COMEX gold futures to extend their recovery towards US$4,200, provided prices remain above the critical US$3,900 support level.

The research house identified immediate support at US$4,000, followed by stronger support at US$3,900.

On the upside, the nearest resistance is pegged at US$4,200, with the next resistance level at US$4,300.

Following the latest breakout, RHB closed its short positions initiated at US$4,284.80 on Sept 23 after the US$4,100 stop-loss threshold was triggered.

It subsequently initiated long positions at US$4,113.50, based on the Nov 5 closing price, with a new stop-loss set at US$3,900.

The change marks a reversal from RHB’s previous bearish outlook, reflecting the improvement in technical indicators and gold’s ability to overcome its immediate resistance.

RHB said it would maintain a positive trading bias as long as gold futures remained above the US$3,900 support threshold, with further gains potentially extending towards US$4,200 and US$4,300.

data.title: Bitcoin Slumps Below US$76,000, Ethereum Plunges 8% As Crypto Sell-Off Deepens
data.description:
Bitcoin and Ethereum suffered sharp losses on Nov 6 as a technology-led rout on Wall Street triggered widespread selling across cryptocurrency markets, with investors retreating from riskier assets.

Bitcoin fell as low as US$75,369 in early trading on Nov 6, down 6.29%, before recovering to around US$76,101 as of 9.35am Malaysian time. The world’s largest cryptocurrency remained approximately 5.6% lower over 24 hours.

Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency, suffered heavier losses, plunging 8.51% to US$2,216.58 during the sell-off before rebounding to approximately US$2,240.

The cryptocurrency downturn followed a sharp decline in US equities on Nov 5, with the technology-heavy Nasdaq Composite tumbling 5.52%, while the S&P 500 shed 4.36% amid mounting concerns over artificial intelligence valuations and potential regulatory restrictions.

Market sentiment was further undermined by lingering concerns over the US$6.3 billion Binance security breach, which prompted billions of dollars in withdrawals and raised questions about investor confidence in digital asset platforms.

The latest losses have intensified pressure on Bitcoin, which has fallen more than 40% from its peak earlier this year. Investors are closely watching the US$75,000 level, with a sustained break below it potentially opening the door to further declines.

Attention now turns to upcoming US employment data and movements in global technology stocks for indications of whether the cryptocurrency market can stabilise ahead of the weekend.

data.title: Asian Markets Sink, AI Investment Fears Hit Tokyo And Seoul
data.description:
Japanese and South Korean shares plunged on Friday as concerns over the future of artificial intelligence (AI) data centre investments triggered another wave of selling across regional technology stocks.

Both Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 and Seoul’s Kospi fell more than 6% as at 10am Singapore time, with the Kospi briefly plunging 8.5% to 4,923 points, triggering a 20-minute trading halt.

The sell-off also spread to Singapore, where the Straits Times Index fell more than 2%. Local semiconductor solutions provider AEM Holdings dropped as much as 13% in early trade, while a semiconductor equipment supplier fell as much as 15.2%.

South Korean chipmakers were among the hardest hit, with Samsung Electronics plunging nearly 10% and SK hynix losing more than 11%.

In Japan, Tokyo Electron shares fell around 9% while Kioxia shed 13%, reflecting broader weakness in the semiconductor sector.

The regional losses followed Wall Street’s steep overnight decline, led by technology stocks. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5%, marking its worst percentage performance since April 2025, as investors reassessed the outlook for AI infrastructure spending.

Investors had initially welcomed the Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections but have since grown concerned that the political shift could bring tighter oversight of AI-related investments, particularly data centre construction.

Online brokerage Monex said concerns over stricter regulations on AI technologies had triggered selling across the US market, particularly in technology stocks.

“In particular, there are concerns that stricter regulations on data centre construction will slow down construction projects,” it said.

Governments and major technology companies worldwide have been investing hundreds of billions of dollars in data centres to develop and operate AI models, making the sector increasingly important to the global technology investment outlook.

AFP

data.title: Kospi Slumps Below 5,000 As Samsung, SK Hynix Extend AI Rout
data.description:
South Korean semiconductor heavyweights Samsung Electronics and SK hynix plunged by around 10% or more on Friday as fears over artificial intelligence (AI) data centre investments spread across regional markets following Wall Street’s technology sell-off.

The Kospi benchmark fell below the 5,000-point mark after opening 2.2% lower at 5,263.63, triggering a 20-minute trading halt just three minutes into the session.

The first-stage circuit breaker was activated after the index remained at least 8% below its previous close for one minute.

Samsung Electronics was down 9.98% at 181,400 won as at 9.14am, while SK hynix plunged 11.71% to 1.116 million won.

Both stocks had suffered steeper losses in premarket trading, with Samsung falling as much as 13% and SK hynix dropping up to 15.3% before paring some of their declines after the market opened.

The sell-off followed a sharp downturn on Wall Street overnight, where the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged 12.25% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52% amid concerns that AI data centre construction could face delays.

South Korean equities had already come under pressure on Thursday, with the Kospi falling 5.28% amid concerns that the Democrats’ sweeping US midterm victory could lead to tighter oversight of AI data centres.

The tech-heavy Kosdaq also opened 3.5% lower at 654.43 before extending its losses to more than 7% within the first half-hour of trading.

data.title: Malaysian Tech Stocks Tumble 5.78% In Global AI Sell-Off
data.description:
Bursa Malaysia opened sharply lower on Friday as a global sell-off in technology and semiconductor stocks spread across regional markets, with the FBM KLCI shedding nearly 16 points in early trade.

The benchmark index fell 15.91 points or 0.97% to 1,619.95 as at 9.10am, giving up gains recorded a day earlier after uncertainty surrounding the US midterm elections eased.

Malaysian technology stocks bore the brunt of the selling, with the sector declining 5.78% as semiconductor counters came under pressure.

Inari Amertron dropped 19 sen to RM2.09, while KESM lost 24 sen to RM4.30 and UWC fell 52 sen to RM6.07. Pentamaster shed 48 sen to RM4.67, while Vitrox declined 64 sen to RM9.96.

Among actively traded counters, Zetrix AI gained one sen to seven sen, while VS Industry slipped two sen to 30 sen and Nationgate fell 16 sen to RM1.71.

The weakness followed a steep overnight sell-off on Wall Street, where technology stocks suffered their worst performance in 18 months amid concerns that a Democrat-led US Congress could bring greater scrutiny to the artificial intelligence sector.

The Nasdaq plunged 5.5% to 1,421.52, wiping out about US$2.5 trillion in market capitalisation. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353 while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 3.44% to 51,523.

Asian markets also tracked the downturn, with South Korea’s Kospi tumbling 7.7% to 4,968 and Japan’s Nikkei dropping 6.11% to 57,346.

Apex Securities said technology stocks were the sector most exposed to further weakness, following the global sell-off in AI and chip counters that dragged the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down more than 12% on Thursday.

The research house warned that the selling could put further pressure on Malaysia’s technology sector.

data.title: Ringgit Seen Trading Sideways Amid US Rate Uncertainty
data.description:
The ringgit opened slightly lower against the US dollar on Friday, with Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid expecting the local currency to trade within a narrow range amid mixed signals from the US economy.

At 8am, the ringgit stood at 4.0450/0520 against the greenback, compared with Thursday’s close of 4.0445/0490.

Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index (DXY) edged up 0.03% to 101.60, supported by signs of resilience in the country’s labour market, with initial jobless claims falling to 189,000 last week.

However, the decline in US Treasury yields suggested markets were less convinced that further interest rate hikes would be necessary.

“Still, the two- and 10-year US Treasury yields dropped 12 and five basis points to 4.46 per cent and 4.83 per cent, respectively.

“This suggests that the markets seem unconvinced about the rate-tightening cycle and perhaps also indicates that the scope for rate hikes has gradually diminished,” he told Bernama.

He also pointed to growing scrutiny of planned artificial intelligence (AI) data centre investments, which are expected to face further examination by the US Congress in 2027.

The sharp sell-off in technology stocks suggested investors were becoming more cautious about the valuations attached to the sector, potentially weighing on market optimism.

“On that note, the ringgit is likely to stay within a narrow band of RM4.04 to RM4.05 today,” he said.

Against major currencies, the ringgit strengthened to 4.5413/5492 against the euro from 4.5428/5478 at Thursday’s close. It also edged higher against the British pound to 5.4421/4516 from 5.4455/4516.

However, it weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5683/5729 from 2.5548/5578 previously.

Against its ASEAN peers, the ringgit gained against the Singapore dollar to 3.1646/1706 from 3.1679/1717 and rose against the Thai baht to 12.0836/1122 from 12.1013/1199.

It slipped slightly against the Indonesian rupiah to 223.7/224.1 from 223.6/224.0, while remaining unchanged against the Philippine peso at 6.42/6.43.

data.title: Wall Street’s AI Trade Takes A Hit As Data Centre Fears Mount
data.description:
Wall Street’s AI trade suffered another major setback on Thursday, with the Nasdaq Composite plunging 5.5% as investors weighed the potential impact of the Democrats’ sweeping midterm election victory on US data centre expansion.

The selloff wiped out US$2.5 trillion in market value from the Nasdaq 100, which fell 6.4%, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index sank 12% to its lowest level in more than six months.

The declines came amid concerns that increased political scrutiny and local opposition could delay data centre projects, threatening the infrastructure expansion underpinning the artificial intelligence boom.

The Nasdaq Composite has now fallen nearly 12% from its record closing high on Oct 6, placing it in correction territory. Thursday’s decline was its steepest single-day drop since the market turmoil following US President Donald Trump’s tariff announcements in April 2025.

“The big election outcome was, especially with the Democrats winning a lot of the governorships, that the slowdown of the data centre buildout is the real key theme that’s going to stick,” said Michael O’Rourke, chief market strategist at JonesTrading.

Chipmakers bore the brunt of the selling, with Nvidia falling 9% and Advanced Micro Devices tumbling 17%. Data centre operators Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN also lost more than 14% each.

The pressure extended to companies supplying power and equipment for the infrastructure boom, with GE Vernova declining 7.4% and Constellation Energy slipping 2.5%. Amazon and Alphabet each fell 2.2%, while Microsoft lost 3.6%.

UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of expected US data centre capacity additions in 2028 could be at risk from potential construction pauses, as opposition grows over the facilities’ impact on local power grids and water supplies.

“There’s going to be a lot of pushback about those data centres being geographically located in someone’s backyard, straining the power grid, straining the water systems,” said Bruce Zaro, managing director at Granite Wealth Management.

The selloff also exposed concerns over financing among smaller AI infrastructure firms. CoreWeave dropped 10%, while its five-year credit default swap spreads widened to a record 1,267.9 basis points, reflecting heightened market concerns over its credit risk.

Nebius fell 15%, with shares in both companies having lost at least half their value since the Nasdaq Composite reached its record high in October.

“The market’s moving from the promise of AI to the price of AI,” said Ted Parkhill, founder and chief executive of Incline Investment Management.

“There’s no question that AI is going to be transformative for the world in the long run. But that doesn’t mean every AI-related stock is currently priced appropriately. There’s going to be a lot of turmoil.”

The Cboe Volatility Index, Wall Street’s gauge of expected market swings, recorded its biggest increase since December 2024 as investors continued to reassess valuations across the AI sector.

data.title: Stock Picks: Mega First And Affin Bank
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB Research) has identified Mega First Corp and Affin Bank as potential stock picks, citing bullish technical signals and improving share price momentum.

For Mega First, the research house said the counter could extend its recovery after breaking above the RM2.75 resistance level and its 21-day simple moving average (SMA).

The stock had previously declined before finding support and staging a V-shaped rebound. Its latest bullish candlestick formation indicated that buying momentum was returning, with the next upside targets at RM2.95 and RM3.15.

However, RHB Research said the positive outlook would be invalidated if the share price fell below RM2.55, potentially opening the way for a deeper correction.

Meanwhile, Affin Bank has broken out of its sideways trading pattern with a bullish candlestick, closing above the RM2.03 resistance level.

The research house noted that trading volume had increased alongside the share price, reinforcing the positive momentum. The counter could next test RM2.15, followed by RM2.27.

RHB Research said its bullish outlook on Affin Bank would be invalidated if the stock slipped below the RM1.92 support level.

data.title: Gold Futures Rebound, Could Break US$4,100 Barrier
data.description:
RHB Investment Bank has maintained its bearish outlook on COMEX gold futures despite a sharp rebound of US$132.60, citing persistent technical resistance that could limit further gains.

In its technical analysis report, RHB said COMEX gold futures surged to close at US$4,073 per ounce, after opening at US$3,940.80.

The precious metal initially slipped to an intraday low of US$3,928.20 before rallying to a high of US$4,081.20, eventually settling near the session’s peak.

RHB noted that the long bullish candlestick, accompanied by a rising Relative Strength Index (RSI), indicated renewed buying momentum.

However, the research house cautioned that gold futures remained below their 20-day and 50-day simple moving averages (SMAs), suggesting that the broader bearish technical structure remained intact.

RHB said gold could attempt to break above the immediate resistance level of US$4,100, but the presence of overhead technical resistance could limit the recovery.

The next resistance is identified at US$4,200, while immediate support stands at US$3,900, followed by US$3,800.

Despite the latest rebound, RHB maintained its negative trading bias and advised traders to retain short positions initiated at US$4,284.80 on Sept 23.

To manage trading risks, the investment bank revised its stop-loss threshold to US$4,100.

RHB said it would maintain its bearish outlook unless COMEX gold futures closed above that level, which would signal a potential shift in the prevailing technical trend.

For now, the research house expects resistance to remain strong, with the latest rally viewed as insufficient to reverse the broader downward momentum.

data.title: Bursa Malaysia Jumps 19.30 Points As BNM Holds Interest Rate Steady At 2.75%

data.title: IOI Corp Edges Up 0.23% After Securing Solar Energy Venture
data.description:
IOI Corporation Bhd edged up 1 sen or 0.23% to RM4.45 as at 3.24pm, with 11.48 million shares traded.

The plantation counter opened at RM4.48 and reached an intraday high of RM4.50 before easing to a low of RM4.43. Its previous closing price was RM4.44.

The marginal gain comes after MBSB Research maintained its Neutral recommendation on IOI Corp with an unchanged target price of RM4.42, following the group’s entry into a large-scale solar venture in Negeri Sembilan.

IOI Corp holds a 25% stake in Bahau Energy Ventures Sdn Bhd, which will develop a 500MWac solar project supported by a 250MW/1,000MWh battery energy storage system.

MBSB estimates the venture could generate RM14 million to RM16 million in average annual income for IOI over 21 years from FY2029, including earnings, land rental and shareholder financing returns.

However, the research house maintained its earnings forecasts pending greater clarity on financing arrangements and project execution, noting that the initial contribution would be relatively modest.

At RM4.45, IOI Corp was trading slightly above MBSB’s target price of RM4.42.

data.title: Stock Today: SkyeChip Falls 2.59% As Shares Extend Decline
data.description:
SkyeChip Bhd fell 7 sen or 2.59% to RM2.63 as at 2.56pm, with 1.55 million shares traded.

The technology counter opened at RM2.69, reaching an intraday high of RM2.69 before slipping to a low of RM2.61. Its last traded price was below the previous closing price of RM2.70.

The decline comes after Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research maintained its Hold recommendation and RM2.85 target price on SkyeChip, citing limited near-term catalysts for further share price appreciation until its growth initiatives translate into meaningful earnings.

HLIB noted that SkyeChip’s core net profit rose 16% quarter-on-quarter to RM18.9 million in 2QFY27, supported by stronger silicon intellectual property (IP) contributions.

However, the research house cautioned that its newer initiatives, including a design engagement with Japan’s SAIMEMORY for its next-generation Z-Angle Memory programme targeting AI data centres, would take time to contribute meaningfully to earnings.

At RM2.63, SkyeChip was trading 7.7% below HLIB’s target price of RM2.85.
